item.text: The NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption provides guidance on recognising and managing conflicts between public duties.
item.support: The aim of the publication is to provide guidance to public officials and agencies on identifying and handling conflicts of duties.

item.text: It examines competing public obligations that affect stakeholders or the wider community, distinguishing these from conflicts involving private interests.
item.support: A conflict of duties deals with two or more different public duties an individual or an agency has that may conflict
item.section: What is a conflict of duties?

item.text: The Commission cautions that unresolved conflicts can undermine impartial decisions, public confidence and the legitimacy of regulation.
item.support: Further, conflicting duties can erode the legitimacy of an agency’s regulatory activities.
item.section: Why is a conflict of duties an issue?

item.text: Its five suggested steps cover identifying conflicts, checking relevant guidance, assessing risks, removing a duty and strengthening accountability.
